articles.title: Anthropic pushes ahead with pre-Thanksgiving IPO despite tech selloff, accepts lower valuation
articles.summary: Despite the tech selloff, Anthropic is pressing ahead with its IPO at a valuation of $1.25 to $1.75 trillion, well below the hoped-for $2 trillion. The Claude developer aims to raise $80 to $100 billion before Thanksgiving. Rival OpenAI has also recently had to cut its valuation. articles.title: OpenAI lands an $11 billion funding round, but has to court dentists for more capital
articles.summary: OpenAI has secured $11 billion in fresh capital, the first tranche of a round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. The full round could swell to $20 billion. That OpenAI is already turning to wealthy private investors hints at a saturating AI capital market and growing investor caution. articles.title: AI Trade Faces a Post-Election Reality Check
articles.summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Yorkville Ives & Co. partner Dan Ives and Bloomberg US equities reporter Natalia Kniazhevich examine the sharp post-election technology selloff, as investors weigh political resistance to data centers, AI spending and the outlook for Anthropic's IPO. They tell hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the election could slow the AI buildout and reshape winners and losers across tech, even as Ives argues the long-term AI investment cycle remains intact. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation: Report
articles.summary: OpenAI completed a substantial funding round, securing $11 billion to increase its valuation to $1.25 trillion. The funding was finalized after the company scaled back its initial plans for over $30 billion. Citing market conditions, OpenAI has encountered shifting investor sentiment toward AI investments and infrastructure costs. Additional funds, which may raise the total to $20 billion, are expected to close soon.

articles.title: Jobs Boom Meets AI Market Turmoil
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." A blowout jobs report fuels expectations for another Fed rate hike, even as Wall Street reels from a nearly $4 trillion tech selloff and mounting questions about the AI trade. Plus, Anthropic's IPO prospects and valuation reset, BlackRock CIO Rick Rieder explains the AI unwind and emerging credit opportunities, Kevin Hassett, director of the White House National Economic Council, discusses inflation and Fed policy, and Greg Ebel, CEO of Enbridge Energy, weighs in on the growing energy demands of AI infrastructure. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: HSBC’s Max Kettner: The AI Trade Hasn’t Fundamentally Changed
articles.summary: Wall Street’s biggest trading desks spent weeks arguing that the stock-market rally would resume once the election was over. On Thursday, that call backfired spectacularly.Max Kettner, HSBC’s Chief Multi-Asset Strategist, argues that the sharp selloff in AI and US equities does not yet point to a fundamental break in the trade. He explains why positioning and forced selling may be driving the volatility, and how he is thinking about AI valuations — including why he’d be comfortable with an Anthropic IPO valuation below $1 trillion. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: The Guardian view on the AI backlash: American voters want a say in their future | Editorial
articles.summary: The tech sell-off exposes fragile promises, while Democratic victories offer a chance to protect workers and hold firms accountableThis week’s midterms showed that the political bill for the AI boom is falling due. The Democratic sweep intensified fears over runaway spending, mounting debt and resistance to datacentres, sending tech shares tumbling. On Thursday Wall Street suffered its worst day since the pandemic as $3.2tn was wiped from markets. Anthropic, developer of the Claude chatbot, is hoping to float within the next fortnight for $1.5tn (£1.1tn), but it may not now get even a trillion dollars. The dominant AI chipmaker Nvidia saw its value crash by more than $400bn. The world’s richest man, Elon Musk, lost $113bn in two days.While a few very rich people may be a little less wealthy, the sell-off may not be a bad thing.
